sentences.en: What was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Well, a lot of our listeners will know, Tom, because they're more sophisticated and cosmopolitan than you are.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们的很多听众都会知道的，汤姆，因为他们比你更成熟、更具国际视野。

sentences.en: That was Welcome to the Rest is History with me, Dominic Sandbrook, and my pitiful servant and slave, Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《历史余韵》的全部内容，我是多米尼克·桑德布鲁克，还有我那可怜的仆人兼奴隶，汤姆·霍兰德。

sentences.en: I thought it was probably something along those lines.
sentences.zh: 我就猜到大概会是这样。

sentences.en: So, Dominic, let's get this straight.
sentences.zh: 那么，多米尼克，我们把话说清楚。

sentences.en: You've never learnt Japanese.
sentences.zh: 你从来没学过日语。

sentences.en: I imagine you've never in your life before spoken it.
sentences.zh: 我想你这辈子从来没说过它。

sentences.en: Tom, you are so wrong.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你大错特错了。

sentences.en: So, we've got a Japanese specialist who's shortly to come on, who will tell you they don't call me, Tom, the master of tongues for nothing, do they?
sentences.zh: 我们马上会请到一位日本专家，他会告诉你们，大家叫我“语言大师”汤姆可不是浪得虚名的，对吧？

sentences.en: We've had Portuguese.
sentences.zh: 我们已经用过葡萄牙语了。

sentences.en: We've had all kinds of languages from me.
sentences.zh: 我已经用过各种语言了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, you have never spoken a word of Japanese in your life, and we have as our special guest, the senior lecturer in Asian history at the University of Edinburgh,
sentences.zh: 所以，你这辈子从来没说过一句日语，而我们今天的特别嘉宾是爱丁堡大学亚洲史高级讲师，

sentences.en: the author of two hugely acclaimed books on Japan, Japan's story in search for a nation, and the Japanese, a history in 20 lives, Chris Harding.
sentences.zh: 他著有两本广受赞誉的日本研究著作——《日本的故事：寻找一个国家》以及《日本人：二十个人生中的历史》，他就是克里斯·哈丁。

sentences.en: Chris, you're still there.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你还在那儿呢。

sentences.en: You haven't run away in horror and shock.
sentences.zh: 你没有因为惊恐而逃跑。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Enjoying myself so far.
sentences.zh: 目前为止我很享受。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Well, thanks so much for coming on, and thank you for braving that.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你能来，也谢谢你勇敢地面对这一切。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So, today's subject, obviously, is Japan.
sentences.zh: 那么，今天的主题显而易见，是日本。

sentences.en: So, we're continuing with our sweet...
sentences.zh: 所以，我们继续我们甜蜜的……

sentences.en: You don't have the courage.
sentences.zh: 你没那个胆量。

sentences.en: You don't have the courage to ask Chris how good that Japanese was.
sentences.zh: 你没胆量问克里斯刚才那句日语说得有多好。

sentences.en: Chris, how good was that Japanese?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，刚才那句日语说得怎么样？

sentences.en: It was pretty good, actually.
sentences.zh: 说实话，相当不错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: No!
sentences.zh: 不！

sentences.en: Get him!
sentences.zh: 抓住他！

sentences.en: No!
sentences.zh: 不！

sentences.en: Tom!
sentences.zh: 汤姆！

sentences.en: I think we should end this podcast right now and start again.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们现在应该结束这期播客，然后重新开始。

sentences.en: The producers should clip that moment and put it on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 制作人应该把那一刻剪下来发到YouTube上。

sentences.en: Oh, my word.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: Unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 简直难以置信。

sentences.en: That's terrible.
sentences.zh: 那太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Chris, so we've asked you on to do basically the impossible, which is to sum up the entire sweep of Japanese history.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们请你来做一件几乎不可能完成的任务，那就是总结日本历史的全貌。

sentences.en: We did a very fleeting episode, didn't we, on Kuba Khan's attempted invasion of Japan.
sentences.zh: 我们之前做过一期非常简短的节目，讲的是忽必烈试图入侵日本，对吧？

sentences.en: And we did two episodes with Ran Amitta on China in the Second World War, which obviously featured Japan as a kind of off-stage bogeyman.
sentences.zh: 我们还和兰·阿米塔做过两期关于二战期间中国的节目，其中日本显然是以一种幕后反派的形象出现的。

sentences.en: But we haven't really looked at Japan itself.
sentences.zh: 但我们还没有真正深入探讨过日本本身。

sentences.en: And I would say that of all the countries in the world whose history I know nothing about,
sentences.zh: 我想说，在所有我对其历史一无所知的国家中，

sentences.en: Japan is the country I would most like to know about.
sentences.zh: 日本是我最想了解的国家。

sentences.en: And it kind of, I would guess that most of our listeners probably don't know huge amounts about Japanese history, and yet we all have this kind of sense of it.
sentences.zh: 而且我猜，我们的大多数听众可能对日本历史了解也不多，但我们对它却有一种模糊的认知。

sentences.en: It has such, its history has such a strong presence in the imagination.
sentences.zh: 它的历史在人们的想象中有着如此强烈的存在感。

sentences.en: Samurai and kabuki and manga and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 武士、歌舞伎、漫画以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: And yet Japan itself, I mean, it emerges when?
sentences.zh: 然而日本本身，我是说，它究竟是什么时候出现的？

sentences.en: Kind of 6th, 7th century?
sentences.zh: 大概是六七世纪的时候？

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想那是对的。

sentences.en: As a unified, the beginnings of a nation state.
sentences.zh: 作为一个统一体，一个民族国家的雏形。

sentences.en: Yes, around the 6th century, early 7th.
sentences.zh: 是的，大约在六世纪到七世纪初。

sentences.en: So the islands have, obviously, they've always been there.
sentences.zh: 所以这些岛屿，很显然，它们一直都在那里。

sentences.en: But what is it that creates Japan as a sort of unified, is nation state the right word, actually?
sentences.zh: 但究竟是什么让日本形成了一种统一的——用“民族国家”这个词真的合适吗？

sentences.en: Is nation state the right word for a 7th century construct?
sentences.zh: 对于一个七世纪的架构来说，“民族国家”这个词合适吗？

sentences.en: Well, I suppose it begins, obviously, centuries before that, even in recorded time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这显然要追溯到几个世纪前，甚至在有文字记载的时代之前。

sentences.en: We have evidence from Chinese records of there being this place, land of the dwarves or various, you know, other unfortunate names that it gets given.
sentences.zh: 我们有中国史料记载，那里曾被称为矮人国，或者被冠以各种其他不幸的名称。

sentences.en: But at that point, it's really a series of small chiefdoms spread across this massive archipelago.
sentences.zh: 但在那时，它实际上只是散布在这个巨大群岛上的一系列小型酋邦。

sentences.en: I suppose what you could say it moves towards, if not a nation state, then one of the chiefdoms or one of these clans, the Yamato clan,
sentences.zh: 我想你可以说，它正朝着一个方向发展，如果说不是民族国家的话，那么其中一个酋邦或氏族，即大和氏族，

sentences.en: starts to be able to dominate and do business with others, really not far from Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto type area for modern Japan.
sentences.zh: 开始能够主导并与其他氏族进行往来，地点就在现代日本东京、大阪、京都一带附近。

sentences.en: And they become dominant clan.
sentences.zh: 他们成为了主导氏族。

sentences.en: They start to talk about themselves as the great kings.
sentences.zh: 他们开始自称为大王。

sentences.en: And this is the beginning of the imperial family that we have in Japan today.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天在日本所看到的皇室的开端。

sentences.en: So, Chris, the actual name, Japan, I learned from your book, The Japanese History in 20 Lives, it's Nihon, which means root of the sun.
sentences.zh: 那么，克里斯，关于“日本”这个名字，我从你的书《二十个人物眼中的日本史》中了解到，它是“Nihon”，意思是太阳之本。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is how the Japanese emperor addresses himself to the Chinese emperor, who is splendidly dismissive, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 这就是日本天皇向中国皇帝自称的方式，而中国皇帝对此表现得非常不屑，不是吗？

sentences.en: He kind of says, do not bring this to my attention again.
sentences.zh: 他大概是说，不要再拿这种事来烦我了。

sentences.en: Presumption has occurred.
sentences.zh: 这简直是僭越。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: In your book, The Japanese History in 20 Lives, you've divided it, obviously, into 20 lives.
sentences.zh: 在你的书《二十个人物眼中的日本史》中，你显然将其分成了二十个人物来讲述。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, let's call it Japan, emerges in the 7th century AD.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们就称之为日本，它出现于公元7世纪。

sentences.en: Who is our first?
sentences.zh: 我们的第一个人物是谁？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the first person really worth talking about would be Murasaki Shikibu, who is around in the late 10th and early 11th century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为第一个真正值得一提的人物应该是紫式部，她生活在10世纪末到11世纪初。

sentences.en: And she is an aristocratic diarist, a lady-in-waiting to the empress.
sentences.zh: 她是一位贵族日记作家，也是皇后的女官。

sentences.en: I think she's worth talking about because this is the point in Japan's history where, after a few centuries of getting a lot of cultural influence from China,
sentences.zh: 我认为她值得一谈，因为这是日本历史上的一个转折点，在经历了几个世纪大量吸收中国文化影响之后，

sentences.en: you know, particularly on things like constitutional law, on poetry, on fashion, on good manners and behaviour,
sentences.zh: 你知道，特别是在宪法、诗歌、时尚、礼仪和行为举止等方面，

sentences.en: Japan is starting to, I suppose you might say, process that and make something distinctively Japanese of it.
sentences.zh: 日本开始，我想你可以这么说，消化这些影响，并将其转化为具有日本独特风格的东西。

sentences.en: And she's famous, isn't she, for The Tale of Genji, which is often described as the first kind of great novel from Asia.
sentences.zh: 她因《源氏物语》而闻名，对吧？这部作品常被描述为亚洲第一部伟大的小说。

sentences.en: That's right, the first novel, or the world's first psychological novel, you could say.
sentences.zh: 没错，你可以说它是第一部小说，或者说是世界上第一部心理小说。

sentences.en: I think she's interesting because she's a brilliant observer of court life in Japan.
sentences.zh: 我认为她很有趣，因为她是日本宫廷生活的敏锐观察者。

sentences.en: You know, we were talking a moment ago about the Yamato clan who gradually managed to turn themselves into this imperial clan.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们刚才谈到了大和氏族，他们逐渐设法将自己变成了皇族。

sentences.en: By the time of Minosaki Shikibu, they've established themselves in what we would call Kyoto now, which is Heian-kyo, back in the day.
sentences.zh: 到了紫式部的时代，他们已经在我们现在所说的京都，也就是当时的平安京，站稳了脚跟。

sentences.en: And she's at court observing, I think what a lot of Japanese would probably say now is one of the high points of Japanese culture and Japanese civilisation.
sentences.zh: 她在宫廷中观察着，我想很多日本人现在可能会说，这是日本文化和文明的巅峰时期之一。

sentences.en: So she's there, she's observing the chapter on her I have, starting off with her diary, actually observing the birth of a child to the empress, Shoshi.
sentences.zh: 所以她身处其中，进行观察。我手头关于她的那一章，实际上就是从她的日记开始的，记录了彰子皇后生子的过程。

sentences.en: It just gives a sense of, I think from her, we get a sense of the vivid religious life.
sentences.zh: 我认为从她那里，我们能感受到当时生动的宗教生活。

sentences.en: You've got this teenage girl on this raised dais behind white curtains in labour, and it's going very badly.
sentences.zh: 你想象一下，一个十几岁的女孩在白帘后的高台上分娩，情况非常危急。

sentences.en: And you've got these Buddhist priests praying, you've got exorcists, you've got diviners, you've got shamans.
sentences.zh: 有佛教僧侣在祈祷，有驱魔师，有占卜师，还有萨满巫师。

sentences.en: You've also got a crowd of people on look as aristocrats gathered around just beyond that curtain to wait for the big moment.
sentences.zh: 帘子外面还聚集了一群贵族，都在围观，等待着那个重要时刻的到来。

sentences.en: So if you didn't have someone like Murasaki at that point, noting this culture for us, remembering it so richly for us, it would just be, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果当时没有像紫式部这样的人为我们记录下这种文化，为我们如此丰富地留存记忆，那它就只是，你知道，

sentences.en: an imperial birth that either happened or didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 一场发生过或者没发生过的皇室分娩而已。

sentences.en: But thanks to her, and also I think thanks to the art of this period, we remember it, I think both Japanese and people outside Japan, as a real classical high point for Japan.
sentences.zh: 但多亏了她，也多亏了那个时代的艺术，我们——无论是日本人还是外国人——都将其视为日本古典文化的真正巅峰。

sentences.en: The kind of time where you probably, one of those two or three moments in Japanese history where you might really like to have been alive and be part of that world.
sentences.zh: 那大概是日本历史上两三个你可能真的想亲身经历并置身其中的时刻之一。

sentences.en: Except for the lack of dentistry, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 除了没有牙科医疗，我想。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So to put that into context, she's what?
sentences.zh: 那么，为了交代背景，她是哪个时代的人？

sentences.en: She's probably, Tom, you'll correct me if I'm wrong about this, but she's roughly about the same time as Ethelred the Unready.
sentences.zh: 她大概是，汤姆，如果我说错了请纠正我，她大约和“无准备者”埃塞尔雷德生活在同一时期。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Is that about right, Tom?
sentences.zh: 差不多是这样吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's not her real name, Murasaki Shikibu.
sentences.zh: 所以“紫式部”并不是她的真名。

sentences.en: We don't know her real name, is that right?
sentences.zh: 我们不知道她的真名，对吧？

sentences.en: Her real name is just lost or was hidden or secret?
sentences.zh: 她的真名是失传了，还是被隐藏了，或者是秘密？

sentences.en: I think it's a testament to the times that women's real names were of not much interest to people, so they didn't tend to be recorded in the way that men's would be.
sentences.zh: 我认为这反映了那个时代的特点，当时人们对女性的真名不太感兴趣，所以她们的名字不像男性的那样被记录下来。

sentences.en: We think probably Shikibu comes from her father's post, Shikibu no Daijo.
sentences.zh: 我们认为“式部”可能来自她父亲的官职“式部大丞”。

sentences.en: So he had a senior secretarial post in the government.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时在政府担任高级秘书职务。

sentences.en: And Murasaki either is a nickname given to her at court from one of the characters of the Tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 而“紫”要么是宫廷里的人根据《源氏物语》中的角色给她的绰号。

sentences.en: While she was at court working as a lady-in-waiting, she was drafting chapters of the Tale of Genji, passing them around for feedback amongst other courtiers.
sentences.zh: 当她在宫廷担任女官时，她正在起草《源氏物语》的章节，并在其他朝臣之间传阅以征求意见。

sentences.en: So some may have given her that name from one of the big characters in the book.
sentences.zh: 所以有些人可能根据书中的重要角色给了她这个名字。

sentences.en: The other possibility is, and it's a bit more circuitous, that Murasaki in Japanese means purple.
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性，虽然稍微曲折一点，是“紫”在日语中意为紫色。

sentences.en: And she was from a very junior branch of the Fujiwara aristocratic family.
sentences.zh: 她出身于藤原贵族家族的一个非常旁支的派系。

sentences.en: Fuji means wisteria, which is, of course, purple.
sentences.zh: “藤”意为紫藤，当然，紫藤是紫色的。

sentences.en: So it's possible that it came via that, as I say, more circuitous route.
sentences.zh: 所以正如我所说，通过那条更曲折的路径得名也是有可能的。

sentences.en: What would be quite significant there, I think, is that she was part of this dominant family.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里非常重要的一点是，她是这个统治家族的一员。

sentences.en: Because although the imperial family, by this point, have written themselves into a semi-fake history of Japan that they put together,
sentences.zh: 因为尽管皇室在此时已经将他们自己编入了一部他们拼凑出来的半虚构的日本历史中，

sentences.en: there are still very powerful aristocratic families with these amazing mansions around Heian-kyo who are vying for power.
sentences.zh: 但平安京周围仍然有许多拥有宏伟宅邸的强大贵族家族在争夺权力。

sentences.en: And the Fujiwara family are easily the most powerful of those, I think.
sentences.zh: 而我认为藤原家族无疑是其中最强大的。

sentences.en: And what she gives us is a sense of incredible psychological sophistication, but also cultural sophistication.
sentences.zh: 她为我们呈现的是一种令人难以置信的心理复杂性，同时也展现了文化上的精致。

sentences.en: And a lot of what she's describing kind of corresponds, perhaps, to the stereotypes that people have of Japan.
sentences.zh: 她所描述的很多内容，或许与人们对日本的刻板印象相吻合。

sentences.en: So among the pleasures that Ulysse Cortes is doing is blossom viewing.
sentences.zh: 比如，当时人们的乐趣之一就是赏花。

sentences.en: And the blossom in Japan is incredibly famous.
sentences.zh: 日本的赏花文化非常出名。

sentences.en: And also you describe how women look at this court.
sentences.zh: 而且你还描述了当时宫廷女性的装扮。

sentences.en: And white powdered skin with rouge cheeks and red lips alongside painted eyebrows and blackened teeth.
sentences.zh: 涂着白粉的皮肤，抹着胭脂的脸颊，红唇，画着眉毛，还有染黑的牙齿。

sentences.en: And that is very much the kind of the stereotype of the geisha, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想那在很大程度上就是艺伎的刻板印象。

sentences.en: Are these continuities or not?
sentences.zh: 这些是延续下来的传统吗？

sentences.en: I think they are.
sentences.zh: 我认为是的。

sentences.en: One of the remarkable things about Japan's history from this period onwards is probably in Murasaki's day,
sentences.zh: 从那个时期开始，日本历史的一个显著特点是，在紫式部的时代，

sentences.en: this is the last era where the emperor in Japan has any real kind of power.
sentences.zh: 这大概是日本天皇还拥有某种实权的最后一个时代。

sentences.en: So listeners will be aware after that, we move into shoguns and samurai.
sentences.zh: 听众们会知道，在那之后，我们进入了幕府和武士时代。

sentences.en: And then in the modern era, we have something that looks like a Western government.
sentences.zh: 到了现代，我们有了看起来像西方政府的体制。

sentences.en: And yet lots of these aspiring leaders in Japan across centuries, in fact, they manage to sideline the emperor or shut them away or whatever they do to them,
sentences.zh: 然而，几个世纪以来，日本许多有抱负的领导人，尽管他们设法将天皇边缘化、软禁起来，或者对他们做任何事情，

sentences.en: they always aspire to some kind of imperial legitimacy, some kind of imperial culture.
sentences.zh: 他们总是渴望获得某种皇室的合法性，某种皇室文化。

sentences.en: So what the culture of Murasaki's era, the aesthetics that you've just talked about, that remains a kind of touchstone for refinement in Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以，紫式部时代的文化，以及你刚才谈到的审美，依然是日本衡量优雅的标尺。

sentences.en: I know that can be almost a cliche when we talk about Japan, the idea of refinement, but...
sentences.zh: 我知道当我们谈论日本时，提到“优雅”这个词可能几乎成了陈词滥调，但是……

sentences.en: We're all about cliches here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里就是专门讨论陈词滥调的。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Well, I think for a culture, maybe there's a parallel with us in the UK here.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为对于一种文化来说，也许这和我们英国的情况有相似之处。

sentences.en: So much of Japanese culture over the centuries comes in from abroad.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，日本文化中有很大一部分是从国外引进的。

sentences.en: So China, later on it's Europe, later on it's the US.
sentences.zh: 比如中国，后来是欧洲，再后来是美国。

sentences.en: So the Japanese come to pride themselves on refining what comes in from Chinese poetry to the transistor and doing something special with it.
sentences.zh: 所以日本人开始以精炼外来事物为荣，从中国诗歌到晶体管，他们都能将其转化为独特的东西。

sentences.en: And if you ask, I think your average Japanese man or woman on the street, what would they say epitomises refinement in Japan?
sentences.zh: 如果你问街上的普通日本男女，什么最能体现日本的优雅？

sentences.en: It's probably the world that Murasaki talks about.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会说是紫式部所描述的那个世界。

sentences.en: You made the comparison with England, so the age of Ethelreddy and Reddy.
sentences.zh: 你刚才做了与英国的比较，也就是“无准备者”埃塞尔雷德的时代。

sentences.en: The idea of a psychological novel coming out of that period is almost unthinkable, unfathomable.
sentences.zh: 在那个时期产生一部心理小说，几乎是不可想象、无法理解的。

sentences.en: How is it that Japan in the 10th century is able to produce a psychological novel?
sentences.zh: 为什么10世纪的日本能够创作出一部心理小说？

sentences.en: It's a great question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: I think probably a couple of things.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有几个原因。

sentences.en: One is the importance of Chinese poetry in Japanese culture.
sentences.zh: 一是中国诗歌在日本文化中的重要性。

sentences.en: So you've got a tradition of reflection, which is aesthetically and emotionally really deep and I think very well established.
sentences.zh: 所以你们有一种反思的传统，这种传统在审美和情感上都非常深厚，而且我认为已经非常成熟了。

sentences.en: The other element is that at court, there's a tradition already by this point of aristocratic
sentences.zh: 另一个因素是，当时宫廷中已经形成了一种传统，尤其是贵族

sentences.en: women in particular, who don't have much by way of a day job because the men are monopolising government roles, writing these diaries, these miscellanies.
sentences.zh: 女性，由于男性垄断了政府职位，她们没什么正经工作，于是就写这些日记和杂记。

sentences.en: So I suppose, say, Sean Ogon's pillow book, people may have heard of that.
sentences.zh: 我想，比如清少纳言的《枕草子》，大家可能听说过。

sentences.en: I think, wasn't it Ewan McGregor was in that film, if I remember right?
sentences.zh: 我记得那部电影里好像有伊万·麦克格雷格，对吧？

sentences.en: He was, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: So I think there's that tradition and it's particularly in women's writing of observing
sentences.zh: 所以我认为存在那种传统，特别是在女性的作品中，她们会观察

sentences.en: people at court and their attempts to be refined and their attempts at one-upmanship in everything from poetry to cherry blossom viewing to clothing.
sentences.zh: 宫廷里的人，观察他们如何努力表现得文雅，以及他们在从诗歌、赏樱到服饰等各个方面试图胜过对方。

sentences.en: I think that's where it comes from.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是它的来源。

sentences.en: That's why Murasaki is so valuable.
sentences.zh: 这就是紫式部如此珍贵的原因。

sentences.en: But, you know, we're going to go on and talk about Oda Na Winaga next.
sentences.zh: 但是，接下来我们要谈谈织田信长。

sentences.en: I suppose the remarkable thing is that some of that can be loSt.
sentences.zh: 我想，令人惊奇的是，其中一些东西可能会失传。

sentences.en: So it's not as though Japan enters what you might call dark ages exactly, but some of that refinement almost completely goes away or it's confined to perhaps the emperor's palace
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说日本进入了所谓的黑暗时代，但那种文雅几乎完全消失了，或者仅限于京都的

sentences.en: in Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 皇宫之中。

sentences.en: And it doesn't really, for many centuries, become emblematic of Japan again.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，它并没有真正再次成为日本的象征。

sentences.en: So Murasaki kind of embodies absolutely the stereotype that outsiders have of Japan as a
sentences.zh: 所以紫式部确实体现了局外人对日本的刻板印象，即日本是一个

sentences.en: place of delicacy and sophistication, perhaps kind of feminine sense of delicacy and sophistication.
sentences.zh: 精致而考究的地方，或许是一种女性化的精致与考究感。

sentences.en: But equally, you mentioned this guy, Oda Nobunaga, if I pronounced his name right, who is absolutely the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但同样，你提到了织田信长——如果我没读错他的名字的话——他完全是反面教材。

sentences.en: So he is 16th century and he's an absolute lad, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他生活在16世纪，是个十足的硬汉，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he is going around kicking sand in people's faces and he's the embodiment of the...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他到处找茬，简直就是……

sentences.en: Is he a samurai?
sentences.zh: 他是武士吗？

sentences.en: He's a shogun, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想他是将军。

sentences.en: He's a samurai.
sentences.zh: 他是武士。

sentences.en: He doesn't become shogun, but he becomes, in effect, ruler of this realm that he's trying to stitch together.
sentences.zh: 他没有成为征夷大将军，但他实际上成为了他试图整合的这个国家的统治者。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I suppose since Murasaki's time in those intervening centuries, what's happened is that the imperial power in Kyoto is on the wane and instead you get these feudal lords.
sentences.zh: 我想，从紫式部那个时代到后来的几个世纪里，发生的事情是京都的皇权逐渐衰落，取而代之的是这些封建领主。

sentences.en: And we start talking about samurai at that point who were vying amongst themselves for real power in Japan.
sentences.zh: 那时我们开始谈论武士，他们为了在日本获得真正的权力而相互争斗。

sentences.en: You have a series of military governments with a shogun at the head.
sentences.zh: 你有一系列以将军为首的军事政府。

sentences.en: And Oda Nobunaga is born into this era of real complete chaos in Japan, civil war between these different feudal lords.
sentences.zh: 织田信长出生在日本彻底混乱的时代，不同封建领主之间爆发了内战。

sentences.en: And he more or less comes out on top.
sentences.zh: 他或多或少成了最后的赢家。

sentences.en: He's one of three great warrior leaders in a row.
sentences.zh: 他是连续三位伟大的武士领袖之一。

sentences.en: He's the first of three.
sentences.zh: 他是三位中的第一位。

sentences.en: And the final one manages more or less to pacify the whole of Japan.
sentences.zh: 最后一位成功地让整个日本基本实现了和平。

sentences.en: 250 years of peace until the West turn up in the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 直到19世纪中叶西方人出现，日本经历了250年的和平。

sentences.en: So Oda Nobunaga, he's a really important, really important figure.
sentences.zh: 所以织田信长是一个非常、非常重要的人物。

sentences.en: But as you say, he accomplishes most of what he does by being extraordinarily bloodthirsty.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他之所以能成就大业，主要是因为他极其嗜血。

sentences.en: A mixture of very bloodthirsty and a really good strategist, I think you'd probably say.
sentences.zh: 我想你大概会说，他既嗜血又是一位非常出色的战略家。

sentences.en: And how typical is he of samurai?
sentences.zh: 他作为武士有多典型？

sentences.en: So for those people who don't know, maybe give us a tiny sense of, you know, I mean, everybody knows what a samurai looks like, but what are they and what's their sort of function?
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解的人，也许能给我们简单介绍一下，我的意思是，每个人都知道武士长什么样，但他们究竟是什么，他们的职能是什么？

sentences.en: Originally, they were, they operated as bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 最初，他们是作为保镖运作的。

sentences.en: The word comes from the verb to serve.
sentences.zh: 这个词源于动词“侍奉”。

sentences.en: So they would serve some of these characters in the imperial capital, Hei Ankiya, who got into all sorts of trouble with each other.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会侍奉帝国首都平安京里的一些人物，这些人之间经常陷入各种麻烦。

sentences.en: You know, you might in the end have a samurai standing outside your door at night if you're a slightly anxious aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你是一个稍微有点焦虑的贵族，最终可能会有武士在晚上站在你的门外。

sentences.en: But over the intervening time, it's much more about honourable war making.
sentences.zh: 但在随后的时间里，它更多地变成了关于荣誉的战争。

sentences.en: There's a blend there, I think, with Zen Buddhism and with the aesthetics of Zen.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里融合了禅宗佛教和禅宗美学。

sentences.en: So by Oda Nobunaga's time, to be a samurai isn't just to go around killing people, it's to have a really good knowledge of Japanese poetry.
sentences.zh: 所以到了织田信长时代，成为一名武士不仅仅是到处杀人，还要对日本诗歌有很好的了解。

sentences.en: He likes to dance and sing from Noel plays.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢跳舞和唱能剧。

sentences.en: So there's a cultured element to him.
sentences.zh: 所以他身上有一种文化素养。

sentences.en: But you wouldn't say that culture adds up to a conscience in his case.
sentences.zh: 但你不会说这种文化在他身上等同于良知。

sentences.en: The standard parallels with knights.
sentences.zh: 人们常把他们与骑士相提并论。

sentences.en: Is that reasonable?
sentences.zh: 这合理吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that's sort of the chivalric ideal of the knight who's, you know, killing people and thinking about Jesus.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有点像骑士的骑士精神理想，你知道，一边杀人一边思考耶稣。

sentences.en: Is that fair?
sentences.zh: 这公平吗？

sentences.en: In the modern era, this was really played up because the Japanese wanted to claim the samurai as being as honourable as the European chivalric tradition.
sentences.zh: 在现代，这一点被大肆渲染，因为日本人想宣称武士和欧洲的骑士传统一样光荣。

sentences.en: But I think there is something there because honour is an enormous part of it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为确实有某种联系，因为荣誉是其中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Hierarchy is extraordinarily important.
sentences.zh: 等级制度极其重要。

sentences.en: And there is an element of a religious sense of sending your enemies into the void.
sentences.zh: 而且有一种宗教意义上的元素，即把你的敌人送入虚空。

sentences.en: So I'd say there are parallels there, yes, to an extent, with Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在某种程度上，是的，这与欧洲有相似之处。

sentences.en: Of course, what knights don't have are the little flag that the samurai wore on their back, which I think is a great tradition.
sentences.zh: 当然，骑士没有武士背上背的那种小旗子，我认为那是一个很棒的传统。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They have it in Ran, don't they?
sentences.zh: 他们在《乱》里有那种旗子，对吧？

sentences.en: The great kind of reworking of King Lear.
sentences.zh: 那是对《李尔王》的伟大改编。

sentences.en: Amazing spectacle of armies with samurai warriors with the flags fluttering over their heads.
sentences.zh: 军队的壮观场面，武士头顶上飘扬着旗帜。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I suppose it's directors like Kurosawa that we have to thank for this interest in samurai to some extent, anyway.
sentences.zh: 我想，在某种程度上，我们确实要感谢黑泽明这样的导演，让我们对武士产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: So specifically this guy, Nobunaga, you said that he's brutal.
sentences.zh: 那么具体到信长这个人，你说他很残暴。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he seems to, he targets his kind of rival warlords and knocks them out of the way and starts to stitch together what will become, I guess, Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以他似乎针对他的敌对军阀，把他们扫除，并开始缝合起后来被称为日本的国家。

sentences.en: And he's also very brutal towards Buddhists, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他对佛教徒也非常残暴，不是吗？

sentences.en: He doesn't like Buddhists.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢佛教徒。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, at this point in Japan, because there's been so much chaos over centuries, some of the big Buddhist sects have armed themselves.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，在日本的这个阶段，由于几个世纪以来一直处于混乱状态，一些大的佛教宗派已经武装起来了。

sentences.en: You've got basically warrior monks on some of these mountaintop temples.
sentences.zh: 你基本上可以在一些山顶寺庙里看到僧兵。

sentences.en: You've also got, if there's a European parallel to bring in here, you've got one sect of Buddhism,
sentences.zh: 如果你要引入一个欧洲的类比，你还有一种佛教宗派，

sentences.en: Jodo Shinshu, which is a sort of Japanese equivalent of Protestantism, rooted in the work of this guy, Shinran Shonin, who's a kind of Japanese Martin Luther, who basically says
sentences.zh: 净土真宗，这相当于日本的基督教新教，植根于亲鸾圣人的作品，他就像日本的马丁·路德，他基本上说

sentences.en: that you don't have to go through all sorts of ascetic practices, etc.
sentences.zh: 你不需要经历各种苦行等等。

sentences.en: You just have one short prayer to say to Amida Buddha and you'll be saved.
sentences.zh: 你只需要念一句简短的祈祷词给阿弥陀佛，你就会得救。

sentences.en: And this is incredibly useful in a fight because Jodo Shinshu can put lots of relatively ordinary people on the battlefield against Odo Nobunaga if they decide to do so.
sentences.zh: 这在战斗中非常有用，因为如果净土真宗决定这样做，他们可以把许多相对普通的人投入到对抗织田信长的战场上。

sentences.en: And some people will carry little pieces of paper into battle with this prayer, the
sentences.zh: 有些人会带着写有祈祷词的小纸条上战场，

sentences.en: Odo Nobunaga, written on it.
sentences.zh: 织田信长，上面写着。

sentences.en: They are fearless.
sentences.zh: 他们无所畏惧。

sentences.en: They come out of nowhere.
sentences.zh: 他们从天而降。

sentences.en: They're quite well funded by local merchants.
sentences.zh: 他们由当地商人资助，资金相当充足。

sentences.en: And for someone like Odo Nobunaga, it's an absolute disaster to have that marriage of religion with armed power.
sentences.zh: 对于织田信长这样的人来说，宗教与武装力量的结合绝对是一场灾难。

sentences.en: So he's extraordinarily brutal about trying to wipe these people out.
sentences.zh: 所以他在试图消灭这些人时极其残暴。

sentences.en: And he doesn't believe in God?
sentences.zh: 他不相信上帝吗？

sentences.en: He doesn't believe in immortality of the soul?
sentences.zh: 他不相信灵魂不朽吗？

sentences.en: Doesn't believe in life after death?
sentences.zh: 不相信死后的生活？

sentences.en: No, he doesn't seem to have any of that.
sentences.zh: 不，他似乎没有这些想法。

sentences.en: He seems to believe in decent security in this life.
sentences.zh: 他似乎只相信今生的体面保障。

sentences.en: So he's got about 2,000 body casts.
sentences.zh: 所以他大约有2000个尸体模型。

sentences.en: He's very Sandbrook.
sentences.zh: 他非常桑德布鲁克。

sentences.en: Very Sandbrookian.
sentences.zh: 非常有桑德布鲁克风格。

sentences.en: I approve of him.
sentences.zh: 我赞同他。

sentences.en: So he, well, he's virtually a dictator, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他，嗯，他几乎是个独裁者，不是吗？

sentences.en: But he doesn't make himself, it never occurs to him, it seems, to make himself emperor, to overthrow the imperial family, kick out the dynasty.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有让自己成为天皇，他似乎从未想过要推翻皇室，赶走这个王朝。

sentences.en: I mean, why not?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么不呢？

sentences.en: Why doesn't he get rid?
sentences.zh: 为什么他不除掉他们？

sentences.en: Because, I mean, they are, you describe in your book that they basically, they adopt him because they don't want to be seen to be cowering before a dictator.
sentences.zh: 因为，我的意思是，正如你在书中所描述的，他们基本上收养了他，因为他们不想被视为在独裁者面前畏缩。

sentences.en: So why doesn't he just sweep them aside and take power himself?
sentences.zh: 那么他为什么不直接把他们扫地出门，自己夺取政权呢？

sentences.en: I think because in Japan, the emperors, this Yamato family that we mentioned towards the beginning, they've worked a myth of divine origins into their story.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为在日本，天皇，也就是我们开头提到的那个大和家族，他们把神圣起源的神话编织进了他们的故事里。

sentences.en: So descended from the sun is the story, is that right?
sentences.zh: 所以故事是说他们是太阳的后裔，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, from the sun goddess Amaterasu in their version of events.
sentences.zh: 是的，在他们的版本中，是太阳女神天照大神的后裔。

sentences.en: And whether, you know, the extent to which people in Japan in different periods actually believe that is rather hard to discern, but there's an aura about them that to go in and
sentences.zh: 无论日本人在不同时期是否真的相信这一点，这很难辨别，但他们身上有一种光环，如果去

sentences.en: commit any acts of violence against them would be the ideal basis on which your enemies could then unite and come for you.
sentences.zh: 对他们采取任何暴力行为，那将成为你的敌人联合起来对付你的理想借口。

sentences.en: You have to pay respects to the imperial family.
sentences.zh: 你必须尊重皇室。

sentences.en: So there's no getting rid of them.
sentences.zh: 所以无法除掉他们。

sentences.en: Some people think that Odor could have easily taken the title of shogun, which is kind of barbarian crushing generalissimo, roughly means.
sentences.zh: 有些人认为织田本可以轻易获得“征夷大将军”的头衔，这大致意味着摧毁野蛮人的大元帅。

sentences.en: I'd love to have that title.
sentences.zh: 我很想拥有那个头衔。

sentences.en: Well, who wouldn't want to be that?
sentences.zh: 嗯，谁不想成为那样的人呢？

sentences.en: Put that on your business card.
sentences.zh: 把它印在你的名片上。

sentences.en: Yeah, but then he doesn't really need to do that because he's got enough real power that titles don't mean terribly much.
sentences.zh: 是的，但他其实不需要那样做，因为他拥有足够的实际权力，头衔并不意味着什么。

sentences.en: He's a man, his entire life, he's always on the move.
sentences.zh: 他这个人，一生都在奔波。

sentences.en: He's always looking to see where the next battle is to be fought and won.
sentences.zh: 他总是盯着下一场战斗在哪里打，在哪里赢。

sentences.en: He's not terribly interested in sitting still in Kyoto and getting on with the administration.
sentences.zh: 他对坐在京都处理行政事务并不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: There's actually still a fair amount of Japan left to be conquered by the time he dies.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在他去世时，日本还有相当一部分领土有待征服。

sentences.en: So he still had plenty on his plate.
sentences.zh: 所以他手头还有很多事情要做。

sentences.en: And he comes to a fairly sticky end, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他结局相当凄惨，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't sort of ride off into the sunset to the cheers of the Japanese people, does he?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他并没有在欢呼声中骑马走向夕阳，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And I suppose it's not exactly spoilers if it happened, what, 500 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我想如果这发生在500年前，这不算剧透。

sentences.en: But he finds himself surrounded by his enemies, people who were allies.
sentences.zh: 但他发现自己被敌人包围了，那些曾经是盟友的人。

sentences.en: It's this guy called Akechi Mitsuhide, who, with his troops, turns on him, sets fire to the temple where Oda Nobunaga, some of his closest allies, are holed up.
sentences.zh: 就是那个叫明智光秀的人，他带着军队反戈一击，放火烧了织田信长和他一些最亲密的盟友藏身的寺庙。

sentences.en: And the thing completely burns to the ground and he takes his life inside, crying treason at the last minute.
sentences.zh: 整个建筑被烧毁，他在最后一刻高喊着叛逆，在里面自尽了。

sentences.en: Some would say that he did very similar things to a large number of his enemies.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说，他对许多敌人也做了类似的事情。

sentences.en: So there's a certain amount of comeuppance in that.
sentences.zh: 所以这在某种程度上是报应。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, he was still young.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，他还是很年轻。

sentences.en: He could have done a great deal more if he'd survived, but that's not the way it went.
sentences.zh: 如果他活下来，他本可以做得更多，但事情并没有那样发展。

sentences.en: That, just a very quick point before we move on, that thing of taking your own life.
sentences.zh: 在继续之前，有一个非常简短的观点，关于自杀这件事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That happens to a few of the people in your book.
sentences.zh: 你书中的几个人都发生了这种情况。

sentences.en: So you have 20 lives.
sentences.zh: 所以你有20个人生。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And more than a few of them take their own lives.
sentences.zh: 其中不止几个人自杀了。

sentences.en: So the Western stereotype is that the Japanese, you know, can't wait to take their own lives.
sentences.zh: 所以西方的刻板印象是，日本人迫不及待地想自杀。

sentences.en: They're sort of like, they're Roman generals.
sentences.zh: 他们有点像罗马将军。

sentences.en: Disembowel themselves with a sword.
sentences.zh: 用剑剖腹。

sentences.en: They're like Roman generals in the sort of first century BC or something.
sentences.zh: 他们就像公元前一世纪左右的罗马将军。

sentences.en: Only one defeat away from a sort of noble end.
sentences.zh: 离高贵的结局只有一次失败之遥。

sentences.en: Is that a fair comparison or is it something that we, is that sort of orientalizing perspective?
sentences.zh: 这是一个公平的比较，还是我们的一种东方主义视角？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't think it is terribly fair.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不太公平。

sentences.en: It's certainly true that there isn't the same kind of philosophical or theological objection to taking your life that you might find in a Christian culture.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定的是，在基督教文化中，对自杀并没有同样的哲学或神学上的反对意见。

sentences.en: There's no idea that it's a sin.
sentences.zh: 没有这是一种罪的想法。

sentences.en: There are a range of reasons why you might do it, including taking responsibility for something,
sentences.zh: 你可能会这样做有多种原因，包括为某事承担责任，

sentences.en: taking your life at or after the death of your Lord, as well as, you know, all the way across to real despair.
sentences.zh: 在你的主公死后自杀，以及一直到真正的绝望。

sentences.en: So there are probably a broader range of reasons why you might do it, but I would say that's not the same as being desperately eager to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会这样做的原因可能更广泛，但我认为这并不等同于绝望地渴望这样做。

sentences.en: I say, Chris, you quote a playground verse about Nobunaga and his immediate heirs.
sentences.zh: 我说，克里斯，你引用了一首关于信长和他直接继承人的童谣。

sentences.en: So Nobunaga pounded the rice, Hideyoshi baked the cake, and Ieyasu ate it.
sentences.zh: 织田捣米，秀吉做饼，家康吃饼。

sentences.en: So Ieyasu basically inherits this emperor of Japan that his two predecessors have pounded and baked.
sentences.zh: 所以家康基本上继承了这个被他的两位前任捣碎并做好的日本帝国。

sentences.en: And Ieyasu is the Tokugawa, as in the Tokugawa shogunate.
sentences.zh: 而家康就是德川，也就是德川幕府。

sentences.en: And the Tokugawa shogunate, it keeps the Europeans out, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 德川幕府把欧洲人拒之门外，对吧？

sentences.en: And it establishes this kind of hermit peace.
sentences.zh: 它建立了一种隐士般的和平。

sentences.en: And it's probably the image of Japan, perhaps, that most popularly dominates people's sense of the history of Japan, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为这大概就是人们对日本历史最普遍的印象吗？

sentences.en: I think possibly.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有可能。

sentences.en: It's inevitable, I think, isn't it, that we see Japan's history from a
sentences.zh: 我想，我们从某种角度来看待日本历史是不可避免的，对吧？

sentences.en: Western perspective.
sentences.zh: 西方视角。

sentences.en: So from a Western perspective, the Japanese in this era, and we're talking about
sentences.zh: 所以从西方视角来看，这一时期的日本人——我们指的是

sentences.en: early 1600s through to middle of the 1800s, were not interested in doing business with most European countries.
sentences.zh: 17世纪初到19世纪中叶——对与大多数欧洲国家做生意并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Because what is it?
sentences.zh: 因为这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: It's just the Dutch go to Nagasaki, is it something?
sentences.zh: 只是荷兰人去长崎，是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's just the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 是的，只有荷兰人。

sentences.en: And I think from the Japanese point of view, it makes an enormous amount of sense.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为从日本人的角度来看，这非常有道理。

sentences.en: They've just been through a few decades of having Jesuit missionaries making large amounts of converts, meddling in their politics.
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚经历了数十年的耶稣会传教士大量招募信徒，并干预他们的政治。

sentences.en: Some of these feudal lords actually convert to
sentences.zh: 其中一些封建领主甚至皈依了

sentences.en: Christianity.
sentences.zh: 基督教。

sentences.en: And it's not really clear where their loyalties lie when they do that.
sentences.zh: 当他们这样做时，他们的忠诚度并不明确。

sentences.en: And so for the Japanese, the money to be made from trade weighed up against the meddling from imperial powers like Portugal and Spain.
sentences.zh: 所以对日本人来说，贸易带来的金钱与葡萄牙和西班牙等帝国列强的干预相比。

sentences.en: It's really a no-brainer.
sentences.zh: 这确实是个显而易见的选择。

sentences.en: It makes much more sense to keep them out.
sentences.zh: 把他们拒之门外更有意义。

sentences.en: And the Dutch, who are expressly against the idea of being in Japan for any kind of religious reasons, they're purely traders, they would say to the Japanese.
sentences.zh: 而荷兰人，他们明确表示不因任何宗教原因留在日本，他们会告诉日本人，他们纯粹是商人。

sentences.en: It's just the Dutch, and they're kept on this tiny artificial island called Dejima, a few feet off the coast of Nagasaki, linked by a guarded bridge.
sentences.zh: 只有荷兰人，而且他们被限制在长崎海岸外几英尺处一个叫出岛的人工小岛上，通过一座有守卫的桥连接。

sentences.en: And they're treated kindly, but they're of little interest to the Japanese.
sentences.zh: 他们受到礼遇，但日本人对他们没什么兴趣。

sentences.en: So there is a sense from a Western point of view that the Japanese are cutting themselves off.
sentences.zh: 所以从西方观点来看，有一种日本人正在自我封闭的感觉。

sentences.en: But actually from the inside of Japan, they're trading with Southeast Asia, they're trading with Korea, with China.
sentences.zh: 但实际上从日本内部来看，他们正在与东南亚、韩国、中国进行贸易。

sentences.en: And it's probably a second great era on which a lot of Japanese now would look back with with pride and happiness.
sentences.zh: 这可能是第二个伟大的时代，很多日本人现在回首往事时会感到自豪和幸福。

sentences.en: Tom, the Japanese treat the Dutch the same way that I do.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，日本人对待荷兰人的方式和我对待你的方式一样。

sentences.en: Kindly, but with little intereSt.
sentences.zh: 礼貌，但没什么兴趣。

sentences.en: Yes, you are indeed a shogun.
sentences.zh: 是的，你确实是一位幕府将军。

sentences.en: As the representative figure of this period, you have chosen another writer.
sentences.zh: 作为这一时期的代表人物，你选择了另一位作家。

sentences.en: And this is Ihara Saikaku.
sentences.zh: 那就是井原西鹤。

sentences.en: Have I pronounced that right?
sentences.zh: 我发音对吗？

sentences.en: Yes, Ihara Saikaku.
sentences.zh: 是的，井原西鹤。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So why have you chosen him?
sentences.zh: 那你为什么选择他？

sentences.en: One of the things I wanted to do in the book is try to give people a flavor of some of the literature and the art from this period, rather than just narrate the historical basics.
sentences.zh: 我在书中想做的事情之一，是尝试让人们感受一下这一时期的文学和艺术，而不是仅仅叙述历史基础。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而且

sentences.en: Ihara is fantastic because he goes early in life, and maybe we'll have a brief quote in a minute,
sentences.zh: 井原很棒，因为他早年——也许我们一会儿会引用一小段——

sentences.en: from writing very beautiful, very moving poetry to creating this fabulous character in one of his books called Yonosuke, means man of the world.
sentences.zh: 从写非常优美、非常动人的诗歌，到在他的一本书中创造了一个叫世之介的绝妙角色，意思是“世间人”。

sentences.en: And it's this young man who sort of tours around all the highlights and the lowlights of Japanese urban culture in places like Kyoto and Osaka,
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人游历了京都和大阪等地日本城市文化的精华与糟粕，

sentences.en: having all sorts of fun, getting into all sorts of trouble along the way.
sentences.zh: 一路玩得尽兴，也惹了不少麻烦。

sentences.en: And it's a lovely way to be, as it were, given a tour of Japan in the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很好的方式，可以让你领略17世纪的日本。

sentences.en: He's kind of Casanova figure, would you say?
sentences.zh: 你会说他是一个类似卡萨诺瓦的人物吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he, just to give you a little quote from one of his, from parts of this book, this is a book called The Life of an Amorous Man, which tells you most of
sentences.zh: 所以，为了引用他书中的一小段，这本书叫《好色一代男》，这书名大概

sentences.en: what you need to know, probably.
sentences.zh: 告诉你所有需要知道的信息了。

sentences.en: It's published in 1682.
sentences.zh: 它出版于1682年。

sentences.en: So yeah, let me give you a short burSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我读一小段。

sentences.en: Um, this is, uh, this is from Ihara.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是，这是来自井原的作品。

sentences.en: The waitress, taking off her linen robe and dainty underwear, threw them upon the fence and slipped into the tub.
sentences.zh: 女侍脱下亚麻长袍和精致的内衣，扔在篱笆上，溜进了浴桶。

sentences.en: She was quite sure that no one was about.
sentences.zh: 她非常确定周围没有人。

sentences.en: If there should be any sound at all, it could be nothing but the sigh of evening breezes among the nearby pines.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么声音，那也只能是晚风吹过附近松树的叹息声。

sentences.en: So thinking, at any rate, she started to rub herself vigorously with rice bran soap and a towel.
sentences.zh: 于是她这样想着，开始用米糠皂和毛巾用力擦洗身体。

sentences.en: The water was pleasantly hot.
sentences.zh: 水热得恰到好处。

sentences.en: She took particular relish in removing the dirt from the lower parts of her body.
sentences.zh: 她特别享受洗去身体下部污垢的感觉。

sentences.en: Suddenly, as though by instinct, she looked up and there on the tiled roof of the tea house next door, she saw the crouching figure of the boy, Yonosuke, levelling
sentences.zh: 突然，她仿佛出于本能抬头看去，只见隔壁茶馆的瓦顶上，那个叫世之介的男孩正蹲在那里，用

sentences.en: a long spyglass at her.
sentences.zh: 一架长望远镜对着她。

sentences.en: So this is him from very early on in his life, but it gives you a sense of what his interests are.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他早年的事，但这让你了解他的兴趣所在。

sentences.en: But also, I think in that quote, you can, if we sort of think back to that really refined period of Murasaki, what Ihara does in his work is he slightly plays on that
sentences.zh: 但我认为在那段引文中，如果我们回想紫式部那个非常精致的时期，井原在他的作品中所做的是，他稍微戏仿了

sentences.en: refinement from this earlier period.
sentences.zh: 早期那种精致感。

sentences.en: You know, the sigh of the evening breeze is among the nearby pines.
sentences.zh: 你知道，晚风吹过附近松树的叹息声。

sentences.en: It's all very poetical.
sentences.zh: 这一切都非常诗意。

sentences.en: But then at the same time, he turns it on his head and says, look,
sentences.zh: 但同时，他又将其颠覆，说，看，

sentences.en: Japan in this era, we're having lots of fun.
sentences.zh: 这个时代的日本，我们玩得很开心。

sentences.en: It's a little bit dirty and we're not entirely proud of ourselves, but we're enjoying the benefits of peace, basically, after a very long time of war.
sentences.zh: 虽然有点肮脏，我们也不完全为自己感到骄傲，但基本上，在经历了漫长的战争之后，我们正在享受和平带来的好处。

sentences.en: So this is the romance of the kind of floating world, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是所谓的“浮世”浪漫，对吧？

sentences.en: The floating world is the idea.
sentences.zh: 浮世就是这个概念。

sentences.en: So can you explain about what the floating world means?
sentences.zh: 那你能不能解释一下“浮世”是什么意思？

sentences.en: Because some people will be familiar with that because of Ishiguro's novel, which is called The Artist of the Floating World, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为有些人会因为石黑一雄的小说《浮世画家》而熟悉这个词，对吧？

sentences.en: So yeah, that word, floating world, or ukiyo in Japanese, it was originally a Buddhist term.
sentences.zh: 是的，那个词，浮世，或者日语里的ukiyo，最初是一个佛教术语。

sentences.en: So talking about the fleeting quality of existence and how it was full of sadness and pathos and one shouldn't get attached.
sentences.zh: 指的是存在的短暂性，以及它是如何充满悲伤和哀愁的，人们不应该执着。

sentences.en: But it comes to mean something completely different in this era, particularly Tokyo or Edo, as it was called then, alongside Osaka and Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 但在这一时期，它有了完全不同的含义，特别是在东京或当时被称为江户的地方，以及大阪和京都。

sentences.en: These are worlds where if you're a merchant with a little bit of money, you can get involved in all sorts of pleasures from
sentences.zh: 这些世界里，如果你是一个有点钱的商人，你可以参与各种各样的享乐，从

sentences.en: kabuki to the tea houses to geisha to buying these beautiful woodblock prints, which a lot of us
sentences.zh: 歌舞伎到茶馆，到艺伎，再到购买这些精美的浮世绘版画，我们很多人

sentences.en: probably helps us to visualize, if anyone's seen those prints, the era that we're talking about here.
sentences.zh: 如果有人见过那些版画，大概能帮助我们想象我们正在谈论的这个时代。

sentences.en: So it's much more fun and it's sort of a golden age for Japan that that word denotes.
sentences.zh: 所以这更有趣，而且那个词所指代的时期，对日本来说算是一个黄金时代。

sentences.en: Kazido, which becomes Tokyo, you said perhaps the largest city in the world in 1700, a million inhabitants, and just obviously teeming with fun things to do.
sentences.zh: 江户，也就是后来的东京，你说它在1700年时可能是世界上最大的城市，有一百万居民，显然到处都是好玩的事情。

sentences.en: So you mentioned kabuki.
sentences.zh: 你提到了歌舞伎。

sentences.en: So kabuki begins what?
sentences.zh: 那么歌舞伎起源于什么？

sentences.en: As kind of skits, and then it becomes this increasingly sophisticated theatrical tradition.
sentences.zh: 起初是一种短剧，后来演变成了一种日益成熟的戏剧传统。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it begins more or less as a way of advertising prostitutes so they can dance around.
sentences.zh: 所以它最初或多或少是一种招揽妓女的方式，让她们可以四处跳舞。

sentences.en: So that's a skit.
sentences.zh: 所以那是个短剧。

sentences.en: So Tom Holland, that is just merely a skit.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·霍兰德，那仅仅是个短剧而已。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I think the comedy element is not to the fore there.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那里面没什么喜剧成分。

sentences.en: It's more whether you might like to take one of these people home.
sentences.zh: 更多的是看你是否想把这些人带回家。

sentences.en: Tom once was telling me about high art and it turned out he was talking about those cards that you used to see in phone boxes.
sentences.zh: 汤姆曾经跟我谈论高雅艺术，结果他谈论的是你以前在电话亭里看到的那种卡片。

sentences.en: Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克。

sentences.en: That's probably about the level, yes, for early kabuki.
sentences.zh: 那大概就是早期歌舞伎的水平，是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But, but I mean, it ends up without women, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，它最后没有女性参与了，对吧？

sentences.en: Because there's this incredibly famous tradition of men playing the roles of women.
sentences.zh: 因为有一种非常著名的传统，就是由男性来扮演女性角色。

sentences.en: Was it Onagata?
sentences.zh: 是叫“女形”吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: The woman's style.
sentences.zh: 女性的风格。

sentences.en: That's partly because of the kind of continued worries about prostitution on the side.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为当时对卖淫问题的持续担忧。

sentences.en: But then, you know, men want to take men home as well.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，你知道，男人也想把男人带回家。

sentences.en: So it doesn't make a terrible amount of difference, but it does have that effect on kabuki.
sentences.zh: 所以这并没有造成太大的区别，但它确实对歌舞伎产生了那种影响。

sentences.en: It gives it that quality.
sentences.zh: 它赋予了它那种特质。

sentences.en: I remember the, the first summer I lived in London, there was a big festival of Japan and they had kabuki.
sentences.zh: 我记得我住在伦敦的第一个夏天，有一个大型的日本艺术节，他们有歌舞伎表演。

sentences.en: Am I remembering right?
sentences.zh: 我没记错吧？

sentences.en: That if there are kind of famous dynasties of actors and you shout out their name when they do something particularly amazing.
sentences.zh: 就是说如果有一些著名的演员世家，当他们表演得特别精彩时，你会大声喊出他们的名字。

sentences.en: So it'd be like kind of saying Redgrave or Fox, Cosma.
sentences.zh: 就像喊雷德格雷夫或福克斯、科斯马那样。

sentences.en: Well, he hasn't got a, he hasn't got a dynasty.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他可没有，他可没有世家背景。

sentences.en: I'm kidding.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑的。

sentences.en: I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我想那是对的。

sentences.en: You've got people like
sentences.zh: 你有像……这样的人

sentences.en: Ichikawa Danjiuro, that they are probably Japan's first celebrities because not only would you go
sentences.zh: 市川团十郎，他们可能是日本的第一批名人，因为你不仅会去

sentences.en: and see them, but you might get a woodblock print of their face or a particular famous scene from a play with them in it.
sentences.zh: 看他们表演，还可能会买一张他们的木版画，或者买一张印有他们参演的著名剧目场景的画。

sentences.en: And those woodblock prints, I mean, now, if you found an original one, it'd be worth a good deal of money.
sentences.zh: 而那些木版画，我的意思是，现在如果你能找到一张原作，它会值不少钱。

sentences.en: In those days, it's the price of a snack.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，它只是一份零食的价格。

sentences.en: So yeah, it's, it's properly, it's properly celebrity time, I think in the 17th century in Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我认为在17世纪的日本，这确实是名副其实的明星时代。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We've gone through three of your choices, Chris.
sentences.zh: 克里斯，我们已经讨论了你选择的三个人物。

sentences.en: We've got three more to do after the break, but as we go into the break, I want to ask Tom a question that is from one of Ihara's books.
sentences.zh: 休息之后我们还有三个要讲，但在进入休息之前，我想问汤姆一个来自井原西鹤书中的问题。

sentences.en: So, and Tom, you can have the break to think about your answer and then maybe Chris can give his answer as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，你可以利用休息时间思考一下你的答案，也许克里斯也可以给出他的答案。

sentences.en: Maybe he won't want to.
sentences.zh: 也许他不想回答。

sentences.en: The question is this, which is to be preferred, lying rejected next to a courtesan or conversing intimately with a kabuki boy who is suffering from hemorrhoids.
sentences.zh: 问题是这样的：你会选择躺在被拒绝的艺伎身边，还是与一个患有痔疮的歌舞伎少年亲密交谈？

sentences.en: Come back after the break and Tom Holland will be telling us his answer.
sentences.zh: 休息回来后，汤姆·霍兰德将告诉我们他的答案。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: And probably like me, you are waiting on tenterhooks to find out Tom Holland's answer.
sentences.zh: 可能和我一样，你们正焦急地等待着汤姆·霍兰德的答案。

sentences.en: Would he rather lie rejected next to a courtesan or converse intimately with a kabuki boy who is suffering from hemorrhoids?
sentences.zh: 他宁愿躺在被拒绝的艺伎身边，还是与一个患有痔疮的歌舞伎少年亲密交谈？

sentences.en: Tom, your answer, please.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，请给出你的答案。

sentences.en: The latter, of course, because I don't care if he's got hemorrhoids, but I don't want to be rejected.
sentences.zh: 当然是后者，因为我不在乎他有没有痔疮，但我不想被拒绝。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: There you go.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Is that the right answer, Chris?
sentences.zh: 这是正确的答案吗，克里斯？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, very good.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常好。

sentences.en: Well done, Tom.
sentences.zh: 干得好，汤姆。

sentences.en: So now we know where you stand.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道你的立场了。

sentences.en: Certainly not said.
sentences.zh: 当然不是那样说的。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Chris, give us please your fourth person for Japanese history.
sentences.zh: 那么克里斯，请给我们介绍你选择的第四位日本历史人物。

sentences.en: So I think the fourth one would be the so-called father of Japanese capitalism, Shibusawa Eiichi.
sentences.zh: 我想第四位应该是所谓的“日本资本主义之父”，涩泽荣一。

sentences.en: And he's around for roughly the second half of the 19th century and the early part of the 20th.
sentences.zh: 他活跃于19世纪下半叶到20世纪初。

sentences.en: This is the point during his life where
sentences.zh: 这是他生命中的一个阶段，当时

sentences.en: Japan is more or less forced actually to reopen to the West treaties slightly along the lines of those
sentences.zh: 日本或多或少被迫重新向西方开放，条约的内容与

sentences.en: with China after the Opium War, if you've just come out of a China program, which are not at all
sentences.zh: 鸦片战争后与中国签订的条约有些类似，如果你刚听完中国史节目的话，这些条约完全

sentences.en: to Japan's benefit, but forced on them really kind of gunboat diplomacy by the Americans, British,
sentences.zh: 对日本没有好处，而是由美国、英国、

sentences.en: French, Russians, and others.
sentences.zh: 法国、俄国和其他国家通过炮舰外交强加给他们的。

sentences.en: And he's interesting because he covers this period after these treaties, which are 1850s into the early 1860s, where Japan is acutely aware of its vulnerability in the world.
sentences.zh: 他之所以有趣，是因为他涵盖了这些条约签订后的时期，即19世纪50年代到60年代初，当时日本敏锐地意识到了自己在世界上的脆弱性。

sentences.en: And it's asking, how can it possibly catch up?
sentences.zh: 它在问，它怎么可能赶得上？

sentences.en: How can it defend itself?
sentences.zh: 它该如何保卫自己？

sentences.en: How can it avoid the fate of
sentences.zh: 它该如何避免那种命运，

sentences.en: China, you know, which just next door is being essentially carved up by some of the big world powers?
sentences.zh: 也就是隔壁的中国，正被世界列强瓜分殆尽的命运？

sentences.en: And he also, he lives through probably the key event in Japanese history in the 19th century, which is the Meiji Restoration.
sentences.zh: 而且他本人也亲历了19世纪日本历史上最重要的事件，即明治维新。

sentences.en: And so that is 1868.
sentences.zh: 那是在1868年。

sentences.en: And that is when the Tokugawa
sentences.zh: 也就是德川

sentences.en: Shogunate comes to an end.
sentences.zh: 幕府终结的时候。

sentences.en: And the restoration is the kind of the restoration of the rule of the emperor.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“维新”其实就是恢复天皇的统治。

sentences.en: And Meiji is the name of the emperor who presides over this.
sentences.zh: 明治就是当时在位天皇的年号。

sentences.en: And am I right that that's the kind of, that's the key pivot really for modern Japanese history?
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗？这确实是现代日本历史的关键转折点，对吧？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are these sort of 10, 15 extraordinary bloody years after the Americans arrived and forced the Japanese to open up in the mid 1850s, where young samurai in particular,
sentences.zh: 没错，在美国人于19世纪50年代中期抵达并强迫日本开国后，经历了大约10到15年极其血腥的时期，尤其是年轻的武士们，

sentences.en: and Shibasawa is probably a good example of that.
sentences.zh: 涩泽荣一可能就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: They are shocked by American technology, the weapons technology, the steamships.
sentences.zh: 他们被美国的科技、武器技术和蒸汽船所震撼。

sentences.en: And they think that the elder generation of samurai in
sentences.zh: 他们认为日本的

sentences.en: Japan simply are irresponsible.
sentences.zh: 老一辈武士简直是不负责任。

sentences.en: They don't really know how to put the country on a strong footing anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们已经不知道该如何让国家走上强盛之路了。

sentences.en: And it gets to the point 1867 to eight, where you have a brief civil war in Japan and the
sentences.zh: 到了1867到1868年，日本爆发了一场短暂的内战，

sentences.en: Tokugawa lose.
sentences.zh: 德川幕府战败。

sentences.en: And you have this new younger generation of victorious samurai who go on to become almost like the equivalent of the founding fathers in the US, I think.
sentences.zh: 随后出现了一批年轻的胜利者，也就是新一代武士，我认为他们几乎等同于美国的开国元勋。

sentences.en: Just on him.
sentences.zh: 就说他本人吧。

sentences.en: So he's called the, what is he called?
sentences.zh: 他被称为，他被称为什么来着？

sentences.en: The John Pierpoint Morgan, is it?
sentences.zh: 是“约翰·皮尔庞特·摩根”吗？

sentences.en: Of
sentences.zh: 被《华盛顿先驱报》之类的媒体称为

sentences.en: Japan by the Washington Herald or something?
sentences.zh: “日本的摩根”？

sentences.en: Yeah, they love to compare him.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们很喜欢这样比较他。

sentences.en: You called him the father of Japanese capitalism.
sentences.zh: 你称他为“日本资本主义之父”。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But I suppose he's a great person to ask.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他是一个很好的切入点。

sentences.en: If you take him out of the story, is Japanese history any different?
sentences.zh: 如果把他从历史中剔除，日本的历史会有所不同吗？

sentences.en: So is he the embodiment of something or is he genuinely
sentences.zh: 所以，他究竟是某种精神的化身，还是他本身就是

sentences.en: a sort of motor of change, if you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 变革的推动力，你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I think he's much more the embodiment because he's one of the first people to go for a joint stock company, to get that idea across to people, to generate the trust where
sentences.zh: 我认为他更多是化身，因为他是最早尝试股份制公司的人之一，他将这一理念传达给大众，建立起一种信任，让

sentences.en: complete strangers might give you some cash on the hope that, you know, your factory might make it.
sentences.zh: 完全陌生的人愿意把钱交给你，寄希望于你的工厂能成功。

sentences.en: Because he's travelled to Europe, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他去过欧洲，对吧？

sentences.en: He's been to France, he's been to Britain.
sentences.zh: 他去过法国，也去过英国。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's had tea with Queen Victoria.
sentences.zh: 他还和维多利亚女王喝过茶。

sentences.en: He goes in the train of a shogun.
sentences.zh: 他是作为幕府使节团的一员去的。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是。

sentences.en: He's one of a generation who do these amazing tours.
sentences.zh: 他是那一代进行这些惊人考察的人之一。

sentences.en: Some of them go literally all the way around the world.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至环游了整个世界。

sentences.en: Fact finding, basically, finding out what makes these great powers tick in terms of industry, weapons, culture and what Japan can do.
sentences.zh: 本质上是为了考察，去了解这些大国在工业、武器、文化方面的运作机制，以及日本可以借鉴什么。

sentences.en: I think if Shibusawa hadn't been around, then probably someone else would have come up with the idea of imitating or adapting the joint stock company idea.
sentences.zh: 我想如果当时没有涩泽荣一，可能也会有别人想出模仿或采纳股份制公司的主意。

sentences.en: So he's much more an embodiment of an era, I think, than he is a motor.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为他更多是一个时代的化身，而不是推动力。

sentences.en: I'm not sure there's anyone in the book who you could credibly call a motor in that kind of great man tradition.
sentences.zh: 我不确定书中是否有人能真正被称为那种“伟人传统”意义上的推动者。

sentences.en: You say he becomes personally involved in 500 companies.
sentences.zh: 你说他个人参与了500家公司。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He helps to set up 100 of them.
sentences.zh: 他协助创办了其中100家。

sentences.en: One of them is Sapporo, the beer, that I'm sure people will be familiar with.
sentences.zh: 其中一家就是札幌啤酒，我相信大家都很熟悉。

sentences.en: He helps to form the Tokyo Electric Light Company, which is Japan's first electricity company.
sentences.zh: 他协助成立了东京电灯公司，这是日本第一家电力公司。

sentences.en: He establishes Nippon Railway.
sentences.zh: 他还建立了日本铁道公司。

sentences.en: So, I mean, he's absolutely Mr. Capitalism.
sentences.zh: 所以，他绝对是“资本主义先生”。

sentences.en: And yet at the same time, he is a samurai.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他也是一名武士。

sentences.en: I mean, as a young man, he studies fencing.
sentences.zh: 年轻时，他学习剑术。

sentences.en: He serves a shogun.
sentences.zh: 他侍奉幕府将军。

sentences.en: I mean, he lives to a fabulous age.
sentences.zh: 他活到了令人惊叹的高龄。

sentences.en: He dies in 1931.
sentences.zh: 他死于1931年。

sentences.en: Is he fusing those samurai traditions with Western capitalism?
sentences.zh: 他是在将武士传统与西方资本主义融合吗？

sentences.en: Are they coexisting?
sentences.zh: 它们是共存的吗？

sentences.en: Is he suppressing the samurai within him to become a capitalist?
sentences.zh: 还是他在压抑内心的武士精神以成为一名资本家？

sentences.en: What's the kind of the balance within him, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为他内心的平衡点在哪里？

sentences.en: It's a tricky one.
sentences.zh: 这很难说。

sentences.en: And there's a bigger question there about how Japan tries to adapt to capitalism.
sentences.zh: 这里涉及到一个更大的问题，即日本如何尝试适应资本主义。

sentences.en: So the claim that someone like Shibusawa would make is that, and this is the claim that lots of
sentences.zh: 像涩泽荣一这样的人会主张，这也是当时日本许多人

sentences.en: others are making in Japan in the era, is that we're not just going to simply copy a Western model.
sentences.zh: 都在主张的观点，那就是我们不会简单地照搬西方模式。

sentences.en: We're going to do it our way.
sentences.zh: 我们要走自己的路。

sentences.en: And what that means for him is capitalism with an infusion of Confucian principles.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，这意味着注入了儒家原则的资本主义。

sentences.en: So the joint stock company isn't simply about people taking a punt and making some money.
sentences.zh: 所以股份制公司不仅仅是人们投机赚钱的工具。

sentences.en: It's about the virtue of cooperation.
sentences.zh: 它关乎合作的美德。

sentences.en: And in his factories as well, he says, look, you know, between workers and management, again, the ethics should be cooperation.
sentences.zh: 他在自己的工厂里也说，看，工人和管理层之间，伦理基础也应该是合作。

sentences.en: Sometimes man and woman is the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 有时他用夫妻关系作比喻。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's, you know, parents and children.
sentences.zh: 有时是父母与子女的关系。

sentences.en: But Japan has to be built on that basis, because if you don't, then you get the slums of London or
sentences.zh: 但日本必须建立在这样的基础上，因为如果不这样做，你就会得到像伦敦或

sentences.en: Liverpool or something like that.
sentences.zh: 利物浦那样的贫民窟。

sentences.en: So he would claim and others would claim that there is a downside to Western modernity.
sentences.zh: 所以他会主张，其他人也会主张，西方现代性存在负面影响。

sentences.en: And because they've been there first, we can learn and do it differently.
sentences.zh: 正因为他们是先行者，我们可以从中学习，并以不同的方式去做。

sentences.en: So it's something obviously that happens in a key moment in his lifetime is the war with Russia.
sentences.zh: 显然，他一生中的一个关键时刻就是与俄罗斯的战争。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In the early years of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪初。

sentences.en: And then by the time he dies, he dies in what, 1931?
sentences.zh: 那么他去世的时候，是在1931年吗？

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So by that point, Japan is already becoming ever more entangled on the kind of Asian mainland, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以到那时，日本已经越来越深地卷入亚洲大陆的事务了，不是吗？

sentences.en: So to what extent is he implicated?
sentences.zh: 那么他卷入的程度有多深呢？

sentences.en: Since he is the embodiment of Japanese capitalism, to what extent is he, by the time of his death, implicated in what we would now describe,
sentences.zh: 既然他是日本资本主义的化身，那么在他去世时，他在我们现在所说的……

sentences.en: I guess, as Japanese imperialism in East Asia?
sentences.zh: 我想，日本在东亚的帝国主义中，卷入程度有多深？

sentences.en: A little bit, because he makes some money in places like Korea, after Japan's annexation of Korea in 1909 to 10.
sentences.zh: 有一点，因为在1909到1910年日本吞并朝鲜后，他在朝鲜等地赚了一些钱。

sentences.en: So he's certainly happy to make the most of those sorts of opportunities.
sentences.zh: 所以他当然乐于充分利用这些机会。

sentences.en: I think the mentality in Japan in this time is, well, look at what any great power does in the world.
sentences.zh: 我认为当时日本的心态是，好吧，看看世界上任何大国都在做什么。

sentences.en: It gets itself an empire for its own benefit and for, you know, for the purpose of spreading so-called civilization.
sentences.zh: 它们为了自身利益，你知道，为了传播所谓的文明，而建立帝国。

sentences.en: And at the same time, if Japan doesn't do it, especially in its backyard, then it's asking for trouble.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，如果日本不这样做，尤其是在自己的后院，那就是自找麻烦。

sentences.en: I think there's that sense of Japan being a prisoner of geography.
sentences.zh: 我认为日本有一种身为地理囚徒的感觉。

sentences.en: If you imagine the archipelago running down just off the coast of China and then Korea, you can't risk the European power or the Americans having effective,
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一下那条沿着中国和朝鲜海岸延伸的群岛，你就不能冒险让欧洲列强或美国人拥有有效的……

sentences.en: or the Russians, having effective control of, for example, the Korean Peninsula, because it's a few short miles off your own coaSt. So that's the kind of rationale that goes along.
sentences.zh: 或者俄国人，拥有对朝鲜半岛的有效控制权，因为它离你自己的海岸只有几英里远。所以这就是随之而来的逻辑。

sentences.en: And people like Shibisawa want Japan to be strong, want Japan to be a leader in
sentences.zh: 像涩泽荣一这样的人希望日本强大，希望日本成为……

sentences.en: Asia.
sentences.zh: 亚洲的领导者。

sentences.en: And I think they're fairly comfortable with the idea of making some money on the side.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们对于顺便赚点钱的想法感到相当自在。

sentences.en: It's always sort of puzzled me that Japan is so successful in this period.
sentences.zh: 日本在这一时期如此成功，这总是让我感到困惑。

sentences.en: You know, they've had the Meiji Restoration, they've embraced capitalism, they are the sort of poster boys for
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们经历了明治维新，拥抱了资本主义，他们算是……

sentences.en: Asian modernity, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 亚洲现代性的典范，我想是这样。

sentences.en: And yet at the same time, there is that increasing, is paranoia too strong?
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，那种日益增长的——用偏执这个词太严重了吗？

sentences.en: The sense of being embattled and hemmed in and all of that sort of stuff, when in a way you could say they should be luxuriating in their success.
sentences.zh: 那种四面楚歌、被困住的感觉，虽然在某种程度上你可以说他们本该沉浸在成功的喜悦中。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's often a claim that gets made in Japan, probably from the 1868 moment onwards, all the way through to 1945, is that Japan is in danger.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这通常是日本从1868年开始一直到1945年都在宣扬的一种主张，即日本处于危险之中。

sentences.en: Japan is in some kind of peril from world powers that don't wish it well.
sentences.zh: 日本正受到那些不怀好意的世界大国的某种威胁。

sentences.en: There's that claim in the end of being encircled.
sentences.zh: 最终存在那种被包围的说法。

sentences.en: You can run right the way around the clock, what, anticlockwise.
sentences.zh: 你可以绕着时钟走一圈，什么，逆时针方向。

sentences.en: You've got the Russians, you've got the Chinese, you've got the British and the Dutch, and then you've got the Americans, you know, to the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 你有俄国人，有中国人，有英国人和荷兰人，然后你还有美国人，你知道，在东边。

sentences.en: So that's often a claim that gets made.
sentences.zh: 所以这通常是人们提出的主张。

sentences.en: And it's hard to differentiate between that being pure ideology and that being a statement of truth, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 我想，很难区分这到底是纯粹的意识形态，还是对事实的陈述。

sentences.en: But famously, so you mentioned Port Arthur, and Japan is the first Asian power to defeat a European power, i.e. Russia, in a war.
sentences.zh: 但众所周知，你提到了旅顺口，日本是第一个在战争中击败欧洲大国（即俄罗斯）的亚洲强国。

sentences.en: And you have a brilliant chapter kind of illustrating the ambivalences and tensions within Japan during this period.
sentences.zh: 你有一章写得非常精彩，阐述了这一时期日本内部的矛盾和张力。

sentences.en: And this is a poet called
sentences.zh: 这是一位名叫……的诗人。

sentences.en: Yasano Akiko, and she is the youngest brother, isn't it, who's fighting, he's been stationed to Port Arthur.
sentences.zh: 与谢野晶子，是她的弟弟，对吧，他在打仗，被派驻到了旅顺口。

sentences.en: And she writes a famous poem that is essentially pacifiSt.
sentences.zh: 她写了一首著名的诗，本质上是反战的。

sentences.en: Brother, do not give your life.
sentences.zh: 弟弟啊，不要献出你的生命。

sentences.en: His majesty, the emperor, goes not himself into the battle.
sentences.zh: 天皇陛下自己并不亲自上战场。

sentences.en: Could he, with such deeply noble heart, think it an honour for men to spill one another's blood and die like beasts?
sentences.zh: 他那高尚的心，难道会认为让人们互相残杀、像野兽一样死去是一种荣誉吗？

sentences.en: And so this makes her both famous and notorious.
sentences.zh: 这让她既出名又臭名昭著。

sentences.en: Famous for the delicacy, you know, with which she articulates her love for her brother and her anxiety about the war that's going on.
sentences.zh: 出名是因为她表达对弟弟的爱以及对战争的焦虑时所展现出的细腻情感。

sentences.en: And notorious because obviously she is offending monarchists and nationalists.
